Subject: RFX follow-up — can you match consolidated seat pricing?

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the runtime consistency and the KV-cache metrics. Procurement asked me to consolidate the vendor economics for an exec review next week. We need a single-line comparison that shows: effective per-seat unit, committed monthly spend, and any seat-tier swap mechanics (we currently have 3 tiers across our org).

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a consolidated offer that reduces the per-seat blended rate if we consolidate tiers into a single seat SKU?
- Are there one-time migration credits (or onboarding credits) you can apply if we contract for 12 months?

I've attached our RFX scoring sheet — it lists current spend and seats by tier. Procurement would like the consolidated comparison by EOD Friday if possible.

Thanks,
Ayesha Malik
Head of Platform Programs
DataWeave Inc.

Hi Ayesha — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the scoring sheet.

We can absolutely produce a consolidated offer that reduces your blended per-seat rate if you move to a single SKU. Quick notes:
- We typically offer a staged seat-tier swap: lower-risk consolidation at T0 (no tech change) + a volume-based rebate applied after 60 days once usage stabilizes.
- For a 12-month commit we can combine an onboarding credit with an elevated committed-volume discount.

I'll loop Connor and Marissa in — Connor can outline the technical assumptions (burst vs baseline throughput) and Marissa will propose the commercial layout (list price, commit bands, rebate mechanics). If you can confirm target committed monthly spend and whether BYOI (bring-your-own model weights) is required, we can turn around a consolidated PDF and a one-line summary for your execs by Friday.

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-28T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: DW-4821 — rate consolidation mechanics

Lauren / Marissa,

Reviewed DataWeave's RFX sheet — some quick technical assumptions to call out for the commercial team:
- Their current mix shows 60% short chats (<=256 tokens) and 40% long-run batch embedding workloads. That tilts them toward needing a hybrid serving profile (low-latency and throughput pools).
- If we ask them to consolidate to a single seat SKU, we should hold a performance-preserving carveout for long-running batch jobs (either priority queueing or separate Dedicated pool). Otherwise their effective costs could increase despite the lower per-seat rate.

Commercial implications:
- Proposal structure I recommend: base list price per seat, committed-spend slabs (0-25k, 25-75k, 75k+ monthly), and a second-line retroactive rebate that triggers at the 60-day checkpoint if usage matches the RFX profile.
- One-time onboarding credit: $35k (to offset migration effort and some egress/storage reconciliation).
- Example blended per-seat math: with a 12-month commit at the 75k+ slab and the $35k onboarding credit amortized, blended unit falls ~18% vs their current blended.

I drafted a quick one-line summary and the amortization table (see attached: Redwood_Consolidated_Offer_DW4821.pdf). Marissa — want to adjust the slab thresholds or the rebate timing? 

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Consolidated_Offer_DW4821.pdf (offer pdf)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-29T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Consolidated offer & next steps (DW-4821)

Hi Ayesha — attaching the consolidated offer and a one-line summary for your exec pack. Summary below for quick paste into procurement slides.

One-line executive summary:
Redwood will consolidate DataWeave onto a single seat SKU with tiered committed-spend slabs; for a 12-month commitment at the 75k+ monthly slab we will provide a $35,000 onboarding credit plus a 10% list discount and a retroactive usage rebate that reduces the blended per-seat rate by ~18% (amortized over the term). Full amortization and slab math are in the attached PDF.

Clarifications and next steps:
- The onboarding credit requires acceptance of the standard SOW milestone (kickoff/validation/hand-off).
- We will preserve a Dedicated-burst carveout to ensure batch embedding jobs do not get preempted — this is a configuration item in the SOW, not extra licensing cost.
- Procurement requested a single-row comparison for the exec deck; the attached PDF includes a single-line CSV-ready row at the top. If you confirm the 12-month commit and expected monthly spend band (estimate you sent looks like 85k/month), we can issue an updated DocuSign with the consolidated SKU and the rebate appendix.

Requested by Friday EOD: confirm commit band (e.g., 75-100k) and whether the SOW milestone schedule is acceptable. Once confirmed we'll send DocuSign and a finalized CSV row for your deck.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps close the loop.

Best,
